"50X The Cash" has one of six top prizes left and is close to selling out. Most of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, the top prizes and the tickets are going at about the same pace.

The table below shows the full count for "50X The Cash", with every prize level included.
981.headline: Where this game is in its run

985.body:
"MAX-A-MILLION" has 448,457 prizes of $30 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $100,000 prize, with six left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

Everything here about "MAX-A-MILLION" comes from official North Carolina lottery numbers, current through October 13.
985.headline: The prize table, line by line

988.body:
The top prize count on "Emerald 10's" has not moved since we started watching it. The game still has two of five top prizes unclaimed. Smaller prizes keep getting claimed as tickets sell. The same top prizes are now among fewer tickets.

Tomorrow's count on "Emerald 10's" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
988.headline: Top prizes are still unclaimed

990.body:
"LADY LUCK" has 142,169 prizes of $2 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $1,000 prize, with seven left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

Every line of LADY LUCK's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
990.headline: What the prize table shows

992.body:
The key fact about "$2 MILLION VAULT" is how its twelve prize levels are built. The prize money leans toward the smaller prizes. Games built like this give out wins often, but rarely large ones. Prize counts change daily, but this design does not.

The table below shows the full count for "$2 MILLION VAULT", with every prize level included.
992.headline: How this game pays out

993.body:
"$5,000 Triple Play" has had no $5,000 top prize claimed for four months. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

The table below shows the full count for "$5,000 Triple Play", with every prize level included.
993.headline: No new top prize claims

994.body:
"$25,000 Triple Play" has 111,690 prizes of $2 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $3,000 prize, with three left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

If you play "$25,000 Triple Play" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
994.headline: What the prize table shows

995.body:
"$200,000 Triple Play" is past the halfway point of its run, with about a quarter of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, a larger share of the top prizes is left than of the tickets, which is a good sign.

Today's free summary of "$200,000 Triple Play" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
995.headline: Tickets sold so far

996.body:
"$1,000,000 Triple Play" can match another game on price and top prize and still pay out very differently. This game is a game built around small prizes that are won often. Of its unclaimed prize money, about three-quarters is in wins under $1,000 and the rest is in bigger prizes. Neither kind is better, and each suits different players.

The table below shows the full count for "$1,000,000 Triple Play", with every prize level included.
